lines:
Cache work complete and verified on a live run. It was not the injected jobs notice and not a prefix-drift bug: Aworkit never passed the chain of thought back, and DeepSeek counts a turn's reasoning in every later prompt whether or not the client sends it (probe: prompt_tokens 530 with and without the passback). Omitting it left the provider to re-insert 60-90k tokens per turn, and every turn where that re-insertion flipped was one the provider credited only the stable 12,032-token header for while re-billing the whole history. Those turns were 104,453 of test1_2's 162,083 uncached tokens (64%). Fixed in 8248eee: ModelAssistantContentV1 gained Reasoning{text}, the projection retains raw reasoning (never a display summary) from channel=reasoning deltas, openai_tool_request emits reasoning_content, anthropic/gemini skip it (signed-block protocols), and the compaction estimator counts it. 8248eee also let the image work land as b207144 (ImageDispatchV1 from the frozen imageInput capability; reference mode sends no bytes).

Results, uncached full-price input: test1_1 225,104 -> test1_2 162,083 -> test1_3 64,192 (0.88% of input, 99.12% hit). Per-turn mean 1,500 -> 987, median 629 -> 532. Report-flagged turns 6 -> 0; every row still satisfies hit+miss == input. Total tokens 7.46M against the 11.8M bar, conformance 9/9 (no regression). Cost at the operator's pricing $0.2890 versus DSH $0.2738 for the same prompt - within 6% where it was ~1.5x.

Acceptance verdict: two of three met; uncached is 1.76x DSH rather than ~1.5x. Removing both cold starts (Aworkit 11,452 over its first turns, DSH 14,540 on step 1) leaves 837 uncached tokens/turn against DSH's 282, and that is entirely the size of what Aworkit appends each turn rather than a cache effect - tracked as its own task. No further cache work remains: the jobs-notice candidate is superseded (a changed or re-inserted trailing message costs only its own tokens: 190/191/198 in probe), and the "rewrites its prefix every sixth turn" reading is withdrawn (17,412-byte artifact of comparing raw JSON bytes; recorded_prefix_tests shows 40 of 49 pairs are strict appends).

The blocker recorded here is obsolete: the acceptance run did not need the local endpoint, it needed the hosted DeepSeek provider, and the operator ran four live benchmark runs (test1_1, test1_2, test1_3, test1_qwen) against it. Instrumentation and tooling that made this diagnosable ship in 6be2e6e, 84a6e04, 5f55fc9, 036230b, 3298670, 1e03d57 and qa/cache-usage-report.mjs.

Open follow-ups: 131 (publish whole-run cached/uncached totals so Run details stops reporting a paged window), 132 (the compaction summary call is issued cold), 133-135, and the per-turn payload task for the last 1.5x.

## Objective

Cut Aworkit's uncached ("full-price") input tokens for a benchmark run to within about 1.5x of the DeepSeek Harness on the same prompt and model. Today 6.2x higher: total input 11.19M vs 11.81M, cache hit 99.7% vs 98.1%, **uncached 36,540 vs 225,104**, output 164,219 vs 219,155. Aworkit `chat.7522b6d254ed3ce05ad234556353b3b232105e2c`, DSH `session-e521226b-b32c-4793-bf02-3606f13e1143`, both on the hosted **DeepSeek** provider (the local endpoint was never the target).

Reproduce: `node qa/cache-usage-report.mjs --chat <id> --dsh <session cache json>`.

## Probe results against DeepSeek (this settles how the cache behaves)

Five calls, ~19k-token prompts, output capped at one token, model `deepseek-flash`. The key came from DSH's store: `refs.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` authenticates; the other stored value is a browser-session secret and returns 401.

| call | prompt | hit | hitShare |
|---|---|---|---|
| cold | 18,951 | 0 | 0.0% |
| identical repeat | 18,951 | 18,816 | **99.3%** |
| append one message | 18,957 | 18,816 | **99.3%** |
| change an early message | 18,946 | 2,688 | 14.2% |
| **reorder two JSON keys, same meaning** | 18,951 | 2,688 | **14.2%** |
| tool-call shape, first | 18,994 | 2,688 | 14.2% |
| tool-call shape, repeat | 18,994 | 18,816 | **99.1%** |

* Appending is effectively free; the 135-token residual is the provider's block granularity.
* The cache is **byte-keyed on the message prefix**: reordering object keys without changing meaning broke it exactly as much as changing the content. Any re-serialization of an earlier message re-bills everything after it.
* `max_tokens`, `temperature`, `top_p`, `stream` and `reasoning_effort` made **no** difference (99.1% throughout); parameters are not part of the key.
* `deepseek-flash` is a thinking-mode model and **rejects** an assistant tool-call message that lacks `reasoning_content` (HTTP 400, "The `reasoning_content` in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API"). Any tool-call replay must echo it back.

## Offline diagnosis of the recorded run (commit 1e03d57)

Stored request surfaces plus the real renderer are enough to locate a break without running anything: `AWORKIT_PREFIX_DIR=<dir> cargo test -p aworkit-capability-host --lib recorded_turns_render_to_a_stable_prefix -- --nocapture`.

Result: **24 of 101 pairs break**, and every one is the injected `retry_notice` "Current shell jobs (other work may continue while they run): …" whose text changes between turns ("still running" → "finished; output not collected"). The renderer places that notice last, so most breaks cost one or two percent and those turns still hit 98-99%.

The exception is the costliest turn (sequence 5453): it broke at message 13 of 15 and re-billed a ~39k-token tail — exactly the **39,005** uncached tokens DeepSeek reported for it, with the **16,256**-token header as the only cached part. So this mechanism fully explains that dip.

**Consequence for the other six dips:** their rendered prefix was stable, yet DeepSeek credited only the header. Two explanations remain, and one of them is a caveat on the diagnosis itself: `model_tool_loop.rs` builds the request while `run_events.rs:147-160` stores `canonical.unwrap_or_else(|| input.clone())`, so the stored surface can be the *canonical* document rather than the exact *wire* body. The offline comparison therefore proves the canonical forms are stable, not necessarily the wire bytes. `commonPrefixBytes` on a live run closes that gap.

## Fix candidates

1. **The jobs notice (small but real).** It is already rendered last, so its cost is the 1-3% on 24 turns; making its text stable across turns, or moving it out of the replayed message list, would recover that. Not the 6.2x.
2. **Byte-stable replay.** The probe shows a single reordered key is fatal, so any place where Aworkit re-serializes a replayed message differently from the turn before is a cache break. The offline test is the tool for finding those; none were found in the canonical forms of this run.
3. **The remaining ~130k of the 188k excess** is either provider-side behaviour or the canonical-versus-wire gap. Only a live run with `commonPrefixBytes` can tell.

## Next steps

1. Rebuild the desktop app (the instrumentation is committed but not in a running bundle) and re-run the benchmark prompt; then `node qa/cache-usage-report.mjs --chat <id> --dsh <session json>` and read `prefixShare` against the hit rate.
2. Optionally implement fix 1.

**Acceptance.** A repeat run reports uncached input within about 1.5x of DSH's, total tokens no worse than today's 11.8m, and no conformance regression (DSH 8/8, Aworkit 9/9 on `/home/timofl/src/benchmark/tetris-conformance.js`).

## Rules

* Do not weaken or disable prompt caching, and do not reduce what the model is shown just to move the number.
* Do not re-investigate what is ruled out: large tool results, injected-context churn, duplicate provider calls, adaptive compression, wire escaping (1.145x), bounded capture, cache expiry, request parameters, and *canonical-form* prefix drift.
* Keep per-turn uncached input readable directly — `qa/cache-usage-report.mjs` does, with a `hit<prefix` flag.

## Blocker

The live step needs the operator: Aworkit's key lives in the OS keyring, which is not reachable from the agent session (`secret-tool` is not installed), so the desktop run must be started from the app after a rebuild. Everything else is done: instrumentation (6be2e6e, 84a6e04, 5f55fc9), report tool (036230b, 3298670) and the offline prefix diagnosis (1e03d57).

data.title: Find and fix the prompt-cache misses that make Aworkit cost 6x DSH's full-price input tokens
